title: Twitch will train Amazon’s AI on your streams unless you find the setting
excerpt: Twitch has added a setting to stop Amazon training AI on your streams. Its product chief says it is off by default because nobody would turn it on.
content_html:
Twitch has added a setting letting streamers stop Amazon using their streams, clips and chat to train generative AI, buried in security settings and off by default. Chief product officer Mike Minton explained the default plainly, saying that if it were opt-in, nobody would opt in.

Twitch has added a setting that stops Amazon training generative AI models on your content. It is off by default, which means the training is on. Chief product officer Mike Minton was asked why it works that way and answered directly: “If it was opt-in, nobody would opt in.”

Minton said it on a livestream this week alongside head of community Mary Kish, after streamer Zach Bussey found the toggle and the screenshot spread. He added that he is comfortable with AI training and would not opt out himself if he were a streamer.

What is covered is close to everything. Streams, past broadcasts, clips, chat messages, and the images and text on a channel page. Twitch’s own example is that a streamer’s voice could train speech-to-text models, improving captions on Twitch and Amazon’s AI products elsewhere.

Chat is where the setting stops working. Opting out protects what happens on your channel, but messages you send in someone else’s chat can still be collected if that streamer has not opted out. Gaps like that have pushed creators elsewhere before, to services built for human artists only.

The framing that Twitch has just started doing this is not quite right. The toggle is new, not the practice. Asked whether their videos had already been used, Minton said he did not know what Amazon had done for model training, and the platform is reported to have been feeding the pipeline for a couple of years.

Opting out also only stops training. AI keeps running on Twitch for chat moderation, ad selection and recommendations, and nothing in this change touches that.

The setting sits at twitch.tv/settings/security. Asked on the same stream why Twitch had not simply emailed people about it, Kish said not everyone reads their emails.

A default chosen because users would refuse it is the textbook definition of a dark pattern. What is unusual here is hearing an executive describe the reasoning without dressing it up.

None of the coverage says how the default works in Europe. That matters, because opt-out consent for AI training has been challenged there before, and Meta had to pause an identical approach in 2024 before regulators let it resume.

content_html_zh:
Twitch 添加了一项设置，让主播阻止亚马逊使用他们的直播、剪辑和聊天来训练生成人工智能，该设置隐藏在安全设置中，默认关闭。 首席产品官迈克·明顿（Mike Minton）简单地解释了默认情况，称如果选择加入，没有人会选择加入。

Twitch 添加了一项设置，可阻止亚马逊在您的内容上训练生成人工智能模型。 默认情况下它是关闭的，这意味着训练已开启。 首席产品官迈克·明顿被问及为什么会这样，他直接回答：“如果是选择加入，没有人会选择加入。”

明顿本周在直播中与社区负责人玛丽·基什 (Mary Kish) 一起在直播中表示了这一点，此前主播扎克·布西 (Zach Bussey) 发现了开关并且屏幕截图传播开来。 他补充说，他对人工智能训练感到满意，如果他是一名主播，他不会选择退出。

所涵盖的内容接近一切。 流、过去的广播、剪辑、聊天消息以及频道页面上的图像和文本。 Twitch 自己的例子是，主播的声音可以训练语音到文本模型，从而改进 Twitch 和亚马逊其他地方的人工智能产品的字幕。

聊天是该设置停止工作的地方。 选择退出可以保护您的频道上发生的事情，但如果该主播没有选择退出，您在其他人的聊天中发送的消息仍然可以被收集。 类似的差距之前已经将创作者推向其他地方，转向仅为人类艺术家打造的服务。

Twitch 刚刚开始这样做的框架并不完全正确。 切换是新的，而不是实践。 当被问及他们的视频是否已经被使用时，明顿表示，他不知道亚马逊在模型训练方面做了什么，据报道该平台已经为管道提供了几年。

选择退出也只会停止培训。 AI 继续在 Twitch 上运行，用于聊天审核、广告选择和推荐，而本次更改中没有涉及到这些。

该设置位于 twitch.tv/settings/security。 在同一直播中被问及为什么 Twitch 不简单地向人们发送电子邮件告知此事时，Kish 表示并不是每个人都会阅读他们的电子邮件。

由于用户会拒绝而选择的默认值是教科书上深色图案的定义。 这里不同寻常的是，听到一位高管在不加掩饰的情况下描述其推理。

所有报道都没有说明违约在欧洲是如何运作的。 这很重要，因为人工智能培训的选择退出同意之前曾受到过挑战，Meta 不得不在 2024 年暂停同样的方法，然后监管机构才允许恢复。
